saints.name: Silouan of Mount Athos

summary.text: The monastery account describes Silouan as a Russian peasant who became a monk at Saint Panteleimon's Monastery on Mount Athos. It emphasizes his long struggle, humility, prayer, and love for others. It identifies Sophrony as the disciple who preserved his life and writings and records Constantinople's glorification in 1988. The source is a monastery's biographical presentation, not Silouan's own surviving manuscript.

blocks.text: Silouan came from a Russian peasant family. His secular life included strenuous farm work and military service. The monastic account stresses the influence of his father’s uncomplicated faith and the tension between youthful passions and his wish to become a monk.

blocks.text: At Saint Panteleimon Monastery on Mount Athos he spent decades in ordinary monastic labor and prayer. His disciple Sophrony recorded a long inward struggle, including periods of desolation and the experience interpreted as a vision of Christ. Sophrony is the named transmitter of these recollections.
